$comment: The authorization vocabulary: what a custom role can be given.
This file is the source of truth. `catalog.generated.ts` is derived from it
and is what the Worker imports, because a JSON import gives widened types
and every guard in this repository has to fail at build time. Regenerate
with `npm run catalog:generate`; `npm run check:catalog` fails on drift.
Two authorities are deliberately absent, and neither can be expressed here.
A super administrator holds the wildcard, decided in `permissions.ts` — so
anything added below is theirs the moment it is added, with no migration and
no backfill. An applicant's access is not a permission at all: it is created
only by verified signup and gates the applicant portal.
Creating, editing and deleting a role, and granting or revoking one, are
absent for a third reason: they are the super administrator's alone, guarded
in code. A pair that cannot be written cannot be granted by mistake.

resources.description: An applicant's submitted file and the casework on it. Reading one includes its case file — its submissions, evidence, revision requests, notes and history — because the workspace returns them together.
Where a submitted application is in its pipeline, and the configured actions that move it on. Which stages a person may act at is decided by the roles that own each stage, as well as by these.
The configured route applications take — its stages, status flags and actions — and which roles own each stage. Changing one changes how every future file is worked.
One round of the programme: the rules every applicant in it is judged against, and the window it is open for.
The questions a cycle asks. Editing them is one authority rather than one per question, because they are authored as a whole.
The order or circular a cycle implements, stored as a PDF beside it.
The banner on the public landing page, including cards not yet published.
The retained history of who did what. It carries more about people than any other read.
An account, as somebody administering access sees it: its address, its state, and the roles it has held.
A named set of permissions and who holds it. Only reading and inviting appear here — composing a role is the super administrator's alone.
Counts and totals across the whole programme, naming no individual applicant.

actions.description: Open and list it, changing nothing.
Write a staff-only note against a file. The narrowest write there is — somebody may comment without being able to work the review.
Bring it into its live state — a cycle accepting applications.
End it on the grounds that it has run its course — a cycle taking no more applications, or an application whose journey a stage action ends without success.
Bring a new one into existence.
Change one that already exists.
Retire a finished round from the working set, keeping it readable.
Withdraw a draft that was never used. The row survives; it stops being offered.
Attach a file, and settle the upload once the bytes have arrived.
Make a prepared version live — an announcement card in front of the public, or a pipeline version for the cycles that open next — or take a card back out of sight.
Take a published item down for good.
Change the order things are shown in.
Offer somebody a role they accept themselves. Bounded by what the issuer already holds.
Take a copy out of the portal as a file. Separate from reading, because a copy outlives every permission that allowed it.
Move a file on from the stage it is at, by a configured action — to the next stage, to the one an input chose, or to the end of its journey.
Send a file back to the stage it actually came from.
Ask the applicant to correct named sections of their form. The file waits at this stage until they resubmit.
Record a value on the file that later stages and eligibility rules rely on, such as the amount approved.
Stop offering it to new work while keeping it readable, and everything worked in it untouched.
Choose which roles own a stage — who may act on the files that sit there.
